principles.how_to_apply: Show a code snippet; ask students to predict the output before running it, then investigate, modify, and create their own variant.
principles.name: PRIMM

examples: Pupil A types, Pupil B reads aloud
principles.how_to_apply: Rotate driver/navigator roles every 15-20 minutes; navigator talks through intent, driver types.
principles.name: Pair programming
principles.summary: Two students at one keyboard, driver + navigator

principles.how_to_apply: Alternate hands-on demos with formal notation; never stay abstract for >15 minutes without grounding.
principles.name: Semantic waves
principles.summary: Cycle between concrete examples and abstract notation

examples: binary = on/off switches they already use
principles.how_to_apply: Anchor new CS concepts in mathematics or everyday language; build up to formal syntax.
principles.name: Lead with concepts
principles.summary: Introduce a new idea using concepts students already know

examples: build a function step by step
principles.how_to_apply: Verbalise intent while typing; deliberately hit bugs and fix them in the open.
principles.name: Live coding
principles.summary: Teacher writes code in front of the class

principles.how_to_apply: Fade the worked-example scaffolding gradually; transition to independent practice.
principles.name: Worked examples
principles.summary: Show a fully worked solution before students attempt

examples: show 3 code blocks, ask which prints 42
principles.how_to_apply: Use mini-whiteboards, exit tickets, or thumbs-up polls; re-teach misconceptions the same lesson.
principles.name: Formative assessment
principles.summary: Mini-checks for understanding after every 10-15 min

examples: 'Would you use a list or a tuple here?'
principles.how_to_apply: Use sentence starters ('I think… because…', 'I disagree because…') to make reasoning audible.
principles.name: Talking points
principles.summary: Structured partner-talk prompts to surface thinking

principles.how_to_apply: Use physical objects / games to ground abstract CS ideas before any syntax.
principles.name: Unplugged first
principles.summary: Introduce concepts without a computer first

examples: 5-min starter quiz on last week's loops
principles.how_to_apply: Schedule 1-week, 1-month, 1-term recalls of every new vocabulary + syntax construct.
principles.name: Spaced retrieval
principles.summary: Revisit prior topics at increasing intervals

examples: stack frame drawing next to recursive call
principles.how_to_apply: Annotate every code example with a sketch of its memory state or control flow.
principles.name: Dual coding
principles.summary: Pair verbal explanations with visual diagrams

principles.how_to_apply: Mix loops + conditionals + functions in practice sets; avoid single-topic drills.
principles.name: Interleaving
principles.summary: Mix problem types rather than blocking by topic
